findings: The provisional branch publishes through SharedBarEngine and range_version, retains incomplete coverage, and is rejected by freeze_e0_ranges before objects are materialized.
The final branch uses the actual RangeVersion parent IDs; source_alias maps those content IDs to the golden aliases only for reporting.
The 13-object assertion is bound to the public objects() producer and checks both exact level geometry and raw instrument identity.
concrete_followups: Keep the existing alias assertion: aliases are reporting labels and must not be passed back into E0Object.source_version.

findings: The correction is appended at a later known_at and a new RangeVersion is produced from a new SharedBarEngine publication; the old context and population are serialized before the revision.
The old/new object sets are compared by their actual content versions and the old serialized bytes are rechecked, satisfying immutability behavior.
The case does not directly assert revised.supersedes on the frozen parent; it only checks the primitive supersedes field and distinct object versions.
concrete_followups: Add assertions that new.range_06_09.supersedes equals old.range_06_09.source_version and that every revised E0Object retains the prior object lineage where the public object contract exposes it.

findings: Zero width is rejected by both freeze_e0_ranges and stop_distance with the golden DependencyUnavailable reason.
None reaches the predecessor-selection contract before any candidate comparison, while an explicitly different prior instrument reaches the cross-contract roll-mapping contract.
The selected objects are derived from actual frozen range objects and then bound to the literal golden birth/known clocks; both signed rows and one background row are produced at every cut.

The policy bridge supplies declared typed E0ActionValue rows and lets score_and_decide_e0 preserve population order while selecting the first equal-value candidate, matching the learned and rule aliases.
Changing a sampled midpoint changes the real population hash and decision-set identity; future labels are not passed to the population builder.
concrete_followups: Retain the explicit check that source_alias returns actual publication aliases only at the reporting edge; do not replace object_version or decision_set_id with golden IDs.

findings: The path_coverage mapping is intentionally ignored by build_e0_decision_population for population construction, so alternate future gaps leave the population hash and no-midpoint reasons unchanged.
The separate native label path carries a typed coverage receipt and its gap is exposed through E0LabelBundle.coverage_annotation; the population bytes are checked before and after labeling.
The helper exercises the one event at the decision cut only as retained source evidence; _label_inputs correctly excludes it from the future path with a strict cut < event_at filter.
concrete_followups: If the case is intended to prove coverage metadata integrity as well as separation, add a negative receipt-mismatch assertion; the current case proves separation but not source_id-to-address binding.

findings: The earlier and later populations are built from separate immutable E0Object values and their serialized earlier rows are preserved.
The future birth and the old object with a future known_at both hit the public known_at exceeds decision cut contract.
The helper sets revised.supersedes but validates the alias map against the computed object hash rather than asserting the supersedes field through the population output.
concrete_followups: Add direct assertions for revised.supersedes == old.version and later[0].object_version == revised.version so the F10 lineage claim cannot pass on aliases alone.

findings: native_path retains canonical events, a NativeCoverageReceipt, provider order, raw bytes/hash, and separate known clocks before label_e0_candidate reads the native quote stream.
The sampled VisitTracker contact is built only from completed midpoint cuts, while reference_object_label sees the native intervening quote and keeps the two contacts separate.
The mixed-stream control selects bbo_midpoint and eligible_trade explicitly, so a native print cannot be silently reused as a midpoint observation.
concrete_followups: Preserve the default bbo_midpoint call and the explicit eligible_trade control; changing either to an implicit union would violate MDS-CANONICAL.

findings: The three variants preserve the declared complete intervals, encode unknown provider order as None in both canonical events and the typed receipt, and route gaps/unknown same-time order through the public object label reducer.
The late MAYBE_BAD_BOOK row is retained in canonical evidence and maturity clocks but is excluded from valid native quote points, which is the intended censored path behavior.
The late variant checks status and maturity but does not assert the exact invalid-book gap interval or the retained receipt recovery facts.
concrete_followups: Add exact coverage.gaps and native_event_ids assertions for the late invalid-book row; add a receipt mismatch negative test if this case is also the source-proof boundary.

findings: The native point at the fixed endpoint is accepted by the <= target-end filter, while the later point is retained in the source path and reported through rejected_event_ids/rejection_reasons.
The typed Target and PathLabel carry the fixed horizon and barrier definition; changing the barrier distances changes both target signatures and target definitions.
The object label control is invoked separately and its departure result is not borrowed by the typed price-path label.
concrete_followups: Keep the rejection reason assertion coupled to rejected_event_ids; a future implementation must not discard the post-end source row merely because the frozen target has matured.

cross_case_findings.finding: NativeCoverageReceipt binds schema, instrument, row count, source order, raw bytes/hash, event intervals, and recovery IDs, but the validation path does not compare receipt.source_id to CanonicalEvent.address.dataset_id and does not reject recovery_complete=False when no recovery identity/certificate is retained.
cross_case_findings.impact: The current INT03/INT05 fixtures use matching source IDs, so the nine cases remain statically compatible; a source substitution or incomplete recovery could pass unless a contract-level check is added.
cross_case_findings.fix: Bind source_id to every canonical address dataset_id (or an explicit registered source alias) and require recovery_complete semantics to agree with recovery_event_ids/recovery_certificate_ids before VenuePath construction.

cross_case_findings.finding: INT03-F03 sets the supersedes field but primarily validates manual aliases and content hashes.
cross_case_findings.impact: A future implementation could preserve aliases while dropping revision lineage and the test would not detect it.
cross_case_findings.fix: Add the direct supersedes assertions listed on INT03-F03.

cross_case_findings.finding: Population/label separation and status outcomes are covered, but the negative receipt metadata path is not exercised.
cross_case_findings.impact: The tests do not independently prove rejection of a mismatched raw hash, source ID, or complete interval.
cross_case_findings.fix: Add one typed NativeCoverageReceipt tamper case that expects IntegrityError or DependencyUnavailable before any label is produced.

conclusion: All nine INT02/INT03/INT05 methods are statically aligned with the public typed APIs and the frozen golden assertions. The two concrete test-strengthening items are revision supersedes checks and a negative native-receipt proof; the source_bridge source_id/recovery consistency check is the only cross-case contract follow-up identified by this read-only pass.
